summary.headline: Nirlon Q2 FY27 total income rose 3% YoY to Rs 174 crore; occupancy held at 99.8% and management opened a sale evaluation of Nirlon House.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was Rs 174 crore (+3% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 137 crore (+3%) at a 78.4% margin. PAT was about Rs 72 crore versus Rs 148 crore a year earlier, but the comparison is distorted by a one-time deferred tax re-measurement charge in Q2 FY26 on moving to the new tax regime. H1 FY27 total income was Rs 347 crore (+3%), EBITDA Rs 270 crore (77.88% margin) and PAT Rs 141 crore. Average occupancy across NKP and Nirlon House was 99.8%, and NIUM India renewed about 37,000 sq ft at NKP ahead of its FY28 expiry.

segments.name: NKP (Nirlon Knowledge Park)
segments.commentary: Occupancy effectively full; NIUM India renewed about 37,000 sq ft in Q2, ahead of its FY28 expiry. About 290,000 sq ft is up for renewal in FY28. Management targets annual escalations of around 5%.

segments.name: Nirlon House (NH)
segments.commentary: Not the primary revenue asset. Management has started a process to evaluate an as-is-where-is sale, as redevelopment is constrained by multiple (14) individual strata owners and 12 tenants.

guidance_outlook: No specific plan for the cash balance was disclosed; management pointed to the historical dividend record.
Dividend for FY26-27 not decided; management said it is too early in November to commit, though FY25-26 dividend was Rs 30 (up from Rs 26).
Dividend policy was revised to allow distributions out of accumulated profits of previous years if circumstances require; management gave no quantum.
Principal repayment to HSBC to follow the facility agreement schedule; Rs 57-60 crore moved to current borrowings with repayment from May 2027, i.e. FY28.
capex_capacity: No capex or new capacity plans were discussed on the call.
About 290,000 sq ft at NKP is due for renewal in FY28; management has not heard from these licensees on renew or vacate intentions.
demand_pricing: Management said limited vacancy reduces the number of live enquiries received; it is confident GCC demand in the Goregaon micro market is strong enough to re-let space at beneficial terms.
Escalation practice has shifted from about 15% every 3 years to targeted annual escalations of around 5%, achieved in part over the last 2-3 years.
Management declined to disclose NKP rental realisation versus micro-market rents and the NIUM renewal rate, citing registered agreements in the public domain.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 57-60 crore moved to current borrowings be repaid in FY27, and will there be prepayments?
qa_highlights.answer: Hong Kong/HSBC loan repayment starts May 2027 (next year). Principal repayments will follow the facility agreement schedule, with no prepayment indicated.

qa_highlights.question: With cash of Rs 345 crore and more to come, will minority shareholders get loan repayment or dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific plan for the cash balances; management pointed to consistent dividend history. FY25-26 dividend was Rs 30. FY26-27 dividend not finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Are tenants interested in the about 290,000 sq ft expiring next year (FY28) at NKP?
qa_highlights.answer: No commitments yet. Licensees will be approached first; if they vacate, management will look at other NKP or external licensees. Hopes for a successful outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Is an outright sale of Nirlon House land being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management has started a process to evaluate potential value of NH on an as-is-where-is sale basis, given strata ownership limits redevelopment.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other income and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income is mainly interest on surplus cash. Management answered 'yes' when asked about sustainability, without quantifying.

qa_highlights.question: What is the escalation achieved on the NIUM India renewal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose it, saying the agreement is registered and public and that terms were consistent with its policy.

risks_watch: FY28 renewal of about 290,000 sq ft at NKP; outcome and re-letting rates are the key operating risk.
Nirlon House sale evaluation may lead to a transaction, but no timeline or valuation was given.
Dividend policy change and cash of Rs 345 crore: management gave no quantum for FY26-27, creating uncertainty for minority shareholders.
Limited vacancy reduces visibility into live demand; management did not quantify enquiries.
Shareholding changes by Brookfield and GIC were raised; management declined to comment.
summary.management_tone: Management was cautious and evasive on dividends, capital allocation, the FY28 renewals and Brookfield/GIC questions, repeatedly saying it was too early to commit. It was more forthcoming on the Nirlon House sale evaluation and on its stated target of about 5% annual escalations.
key_quotes: We feel fairly confident that the existing GCC demand in this micro market will be strong enough to ensure that we can license on commercially what we think are beneficial terms for both licensor and licensee.
